s0.title: Create a profile
s0.text: Click this button. There's no password or sign-up — you only get a code (token) that is the key to your data.

s1.title: This is your token
s1.text: 16 characters. Whoever knows it has access to your data — so don't share it with anyone.

s2.title: Save it
s2.text: Copy the token and keep it somewhere safe, e.g. in your notes. On another device, enter it under “Load profile” and everything will appear. From now on your favorites and trains are saved to your profile automatically.

s0.title: Start here
s0.text: Type the name of any station to check its departures. A district alone works too, e.g. „Załęże” — I'll suggest the full name.

s1.title: Live board
s1.text: Click “Show live data” to see departures with real delays, not just the timetable.

s2.title: Favorite stations
s2.text: Your pinned stations. Add your own with the ☆ star next to the board below.

s3.title: Favorite trains
s3.text: ⭐ The star next to every departure (and in the train details) adds it to “My trains” — from there, at a glance and without extra clicks, you'll see where it was last confirmed at a station and whether it's on time. Add several to follow a whole journey — a one-off trip or your daily commute.

s4.title: More options in one place
s4.text: Press and hold (or right-click) any row — a menu opens with all the actions: details, favorites, calendar and journal at once.

s5.title: Delay alarm
s5.text: Turn it on to get a notification about a delay or cancellation at the chosen station — it only works while this tab is open. If PLK gives a reason (e.g. “Rolling stock fault”), you'll see it under the alarm entry after clicking the small ⓘ.

s6.title: Background alarm for this station
s6.text: 👁 Watch in background — unlike the “Delay alarm” above, this works EVEN with the tab or app closed: you'll get a push notification about a delay or cancellation at this station wherever you are. Requires a profile — push notifications live on the server under your token. Tapping such a notification opens this station's board.

s7.title: Travel journal
s7.text: The menu (☰) has the 📓 Journal — it records your trips along with any delay.

s8.title: Profile and sync
s8.text: Create a token here — 16 characters, no password or login — to sync favorite stations, trains, alarms and the journal across devices.

chat.title: 💬 Ask how to get there (BETA)
chat.text: Write or say 🎤 where you're going, e.g. „z Katowic do Gliwic jutro po siedemnastej” (Polish only for now). Prefer clicking? Choose „🧭 Krok po kroku” (step by step) or type just a station — I'll ask whether you start there and guide you. If I don't understand, I'll ask, and I'll open the results in the planner.

sound.title: 🔊 A real Rp1 from Tarnowskie Góry
sound.text: The alarm sounds like a locomotive horn — it's the original Rp1 signal recorded in Tarnowskie Góry at the last train to Opole (December 2011). Use this button to mute it; vibration stays.

lang.title: 🌐 6 languages
lang.text: The app speaks Polish, English, German, Czech, Spanish and Ukrainian. Pick your language here — I'll remember it, and with a profile on all your devices.

districts.title: Search by district too
districts.text: Type just „Załęże”, „Ligota” or „Płaszów” — I'll suggest the full station name (Katowice Załęże, Kraków Płaszów). Stations in your cities come first.

watchBoard.title: The notification opens the board
watchBoard.text: Tapping a delay notification for a watched station now opens that station's departure board straight away.

guard.title: 🛡️ Guard your connection
guard.text: New in the planner: next to a result tap 🛡️ Guard — I'll watch the delays, warn you with a notification when a transfer is at risk and suggest a Plan B right away. After arrival I'll ask whether to save the trip in your journal.

s0.title: Your trains
s0.text: Here you see the status of every tracked service: delay, platform/track and the last confirmed station. Click a card to see the whole run.

s1.title: Star and order
s1.text: The ★ star removes the train from the list (without confirmation) — click the same star on the board again to add it back. Use the ▲▼ arrows to change the order of the cards.

s2.title: Background alarm
s2.text: Turn it on to get a push notification about a delay or cancellation of ANY of the trains tracked here — it works even with the app closed. Requires a profile.

s3.title: Add a train
s3.text: Enter the station, number and planned time once — from then on you'll always see it here with its current status.

s4.title: Refresh manually
s4.text: The list updates by itself when you come back after a longer break, but you can also refresh at any time.

s5.title: Travel journal
s5.text: Your trips along with any delay — you add them on the train's run page.

s6.title: Profile and sync
s6.text: The profile token takes this list, alarms and journal to every one of your devices.

sound.title: 🔊 A real Rp1 from Tarnowskie Góry
sound.text: The alarm sounds like a locomotive horn — it's the original Rp1 signal recorded in Tarnowskie Góry at the last train to Opole (December 2011). Use this button to mute it; vibration stays.

s0.title: Add to My trains
s0.text: Click the star to keep this service at hand in My trains — with its current status, without searching again. A second click removes it from the list.

s1.title: The whole run
s1.text: The train's entire route station by station: planned and actual times, delay, platform and track. If PLK gives a reason for the delay (e.g. “Rolling stock fault”), you'll see it in the red note under the header.

s2.title: Travel journal
s2.text: Riding this train? Mark 🚏 where you board and 🏁 where you get off — we'll work out the rest. A floating save button appears at the bottom of the screen wherever you scroll. For a service that hasn't reached your exit station yet, instead of saving you'll see “📋 Add to plan” — an entry in the journal's travel plan, not a real trip yet.

s0.title: New profile
s0.text: If you don't have a profile yet, create a new token here with one click.

s1.title: Already have a token?
s1.text: Paste a token from another device here to load your favorite stations, trains, alarms, journal and favorite routes.

s2.title: Unlink device
s2.text: Removes the token ONLY from this device — the data in the cloud stays and can still be loaded with the same token anywhere else.

s0.title: Favorite routes
s0.text: Set up your recurring route once (e.g. home→work) — everything saves itself as you type. Then the app will ask on the train's run page whether to save a matching service. Use “➕ Add another route” to add as many as you like.

s1.title: Travel plan
s1.text: Planning a route (e.g. with a change) and want to check it works before you leave? Mark the stations on each train's run and add “📋 To plan” — you'll see all legs here at once. Once you've actually travelled, click “✅ Confirm” — only then does the trip go to your saved trips, with real times; “❌ Reject” removes it from the plan.

s2.title: Saved trips
s2.text: Your saved, confirmed trips, newest first. You can edit them (🔓) — changes save themselves too — or download everything as XLSX.

guard.title: 🛡️ Your plan is guarded
guard.text: I guard trips from your travel plan automatically: I'll warn you when a transfer is at risk and after arrival ask whether to save the trip. Turn it off in the planner: 📌 Mine → ⚙️ Guard settings.

s0.title: Journey planner (beta)
s0.text: Enter where from and where to — it finds direct connections and ones with changes (even several) based on the PLK timetable, for the whole network, not just selected stations. We're still testing, so imperfections happen. Suggestions understand districts and inflected forms („Załęże”, „z Płaszowa”).

s1.title: Advanced
s1.text: Minimum change time (3 min by default), the “Direct only” option (no changes), forcing a specific “via” station and excluding chosen operators from the results.

s2.title: Save or add to the journal
s2.text: You can 💾 save any result to review later or 📋 add it to the travel plan in your journal — each leg separately. When you actually travel, you'll confirm the real trip in the journal with one click.

districts.title: Search by district too
districts.text: Type just „Załęże”, „Ligota” or „Płaszów” — I'll suggest the full station name. ↑/↓ and Enter pick a station, and Enter in the field searches right away.

badges.title: ⚡ and 🔁 — there's a faster way
badges.text: A blinking ⚡ badge on a result means another direct train arrives sooner, and 🔁 means a connection with a change is faster. Tap the badge to see that connection.

chat.title: 💬 Ask how to get there (BETA)
chat.text: Prefer to write or say 🎤 a whole sentence (in Polish)? The assistant fills in this form for you and shows the results right away — or guides you step by step.

tabs.title: 🧭 Everything about a connection in one place
tabs.text: 🔎 Search, 🛡️ Guarded, 📌 Saved and 🕘 Recent — switch with one tap. When you scroll, the bar stays at the top: the active tab with its name, the others as icons (name in a tooltip).

mine.title: 🛡️ Guarded connections
mine.text: Tap 🛡️ Guard next to a result and I'll watch your transfers: recalculated times, a push warning when a transfer is at risk and a Plan B from the transfer station. Saved results are next door, in 📌 Saved.

recent.title: 🕘 A search from a few days ago?
recent.text: For an entry from a past day you choose: 🔎 today from the same time (or tomorrow if it has passed) or 📅 that day.

dziennik.title: 📓 Travel journal
dziennik.infoTitle: What this is and how to fill it in
dziennik.infoJournal: Save your regular, recurring routes here (e.g. your daily commute) — just fill in the boarding and exit stations once. The journal will recognise when you're travelling one of your saved routes and offer a quick save with the right name for a matching service. If the route has a change, also fill in “Leg 2” — each leg is saved as a separate entry. The “Departure from–to” field is the time window in which we treat a trip as typical; outside it you'll be asked whether to save it anyway. With “➕ Add another route” you can add as many as you like — handy e.g. for different times on different days or for other recurring trips. All of this (routes, entries, favorite stations, My trains) is visible only in this browser unless you create a profile — then you'll see the same on your other devices too. Without a profile (e.g. in an incognito window) the data disappears when the browser closes.
dziennik.subtitle: Saved trips with the boarding and exit station marked — you add them on the train's run page.
dziennik.profileHint: 💾 Changes are saved automatically in this browser. You don't have a profile — without one you won't see any of this on another device, and e.g. in an incognito window it will vanish when you close it. Create a profile — it only takes a moment.
dziennik.tripsNone: Not set up — expand to configure
dziennik.infoPlan: Trips you're still planning end up here — marked (🚏/🏁) on the run of a train that hasn't reached the exit station yet. You'll see all planned legs together, so it's easier to judge whether the whole route (even with changes) works out. When the train actually arrives, come back and click “✅ Confirm” — the entry moves to the journal below with the real time and delay. “❌ Reject” simply removes the plan.
dziennik.planEmpty: No planned trips. On the run of a train that hasn't reached your exit station yet, mark 🚏/🏁 and add “📋 To plan”.
dziennik.notArrived: PLK hasn't confirmed the arrival yet — that's normal, sometimes it takes longer than the trip itself. We'll try again automatically in the background, you don't need to do anything.
dziennik.checkFailed: Couldn't check the status. Please try again.
dziennik.syncFailed: ⚠️ The change was saved only locally in this browser — syncing with your profile failed. Check your connection and try again (e.g. refresh the page).
dziennik.reverseNeedSource: Choose the route to copy the legs from in reverse.
dziennik.reverseNoLegs: The chosen route has no legs filled in yet.
dziennik.leg2Hint: (after the change — leave empty if you travel without one)
dziennik.kmInfoTitle: Why it has to be entered by hand
dziennik.kmInfo: PLK's data includes the timetable and delays but not the distances between stations — so it can't be filled in automatically. Enter the km once by hand (e.g. from your ticket, the PKP timetable or the operator's fare table) — the journal will remember it and fill it in for every later trip on the same route.

jak.title: 📖 Czy zdążę?
jak.subtitle:
A free departure board and delay monitor based on PLK data —
no ads, no login, no app to install.
jak.lede: Czy zdążę? (“Will I make it?”) shows the real train timetable: times, delays, platforms and tracks straight from PLK data — and on top of that it alerts you about delays, keeps an eye on your favorite services, helps plan a journey with changes and keeps a journal of your trips. It works in the browser — on your phone and computer — with nothing to install.
jak.sec_tablica:
🚉 Departure board

Type a station name (or tap one of the quick buttons) and see a live departure board: planned and actual time, delay, train number and category, destination with “via” stops, platform and track.

  • The delay is colour-coded: on time, up to 10 min, 10–20 min, over 20 min.
  • Clicking any row opens the full train run — every station on the route with times and the delay at each one.
  • The ☆/★ star next to a row adds the service to My trains, the 📅 icon adds it to your calendar.
  • The ☆/★ star next to the station name (above the board) saves it as a favorite — it then appears as a quick button on the home page.
jak.sec_alarm:
🔔 Alarm and delay reasons

The Alarm: OFF/ON button above the board turns on a summary: services with the status “delayed” or “cancelled” are listed in one place above the departures, so you don't have to scan the whole board.

  • If PLK provides the reason for a disruption (e.g. “Rolling stock fault”, “Signalling equipment failure”), you'll see it after tapping the small ⓘ icon at the end of the alarm row — it expands below.
  • The reason is fetched not only from the station you're at — if the train is already delayed before it gets there, you'll see it too.
  • Not every delay has a reason — sometimes the dispatcher simply didn't enter one. That's not an app bug, just the state of the source data.
jak.sec_menu:
👆 Row context menu

Press and hold any row on the board (or right-click it on a computer) — a menu with all the actions opens at once:

  • Train details — the full run of the route.
  • Add / remove from favorites — the same as the star in the row.
  • Add to calendar — a ready event with the departure time.
  • Add to the journal as a typical route — appears only when this service matches one of your saved favorite routes — saved with one click, without going to the train run page.
  • Add to the journal with editing — takes you to the train run page with the boarding station already marked; you only need to pick where you get off.
jak.sec_moje_pociagi:
⭐ My trains

A list of services you follow permanently — e.g. your daily commute or several trains of one longer journey. Each card looks like a row on the board (same colours and layout) and also shows the train's last confirmed station.

  • The ★ star removes the service from the list immediately, without asking for confirmation — on the board just click the same star again to add it back.
  • Use the ▲▼ arrows to set your own order of cards.
  • Clicking a card opens the full train run.
jak.sec_bieg:
🛤️ Train run

The full route of the chosen service: every station in order, planned and actual time at each, the current delay and — if PLK provides it — the reason for the disruption in a red box at the top of the page.

  • The star next to the train number adds it to My trains (a second click removes it).
  • The 🚏 (boarding) and 🏁 (exit) icons next to stations mark your part of the journey.
  • Once both stations are marked, a floating button for saving to the journal appears at the bottom of the screen — it stays visible while you scroll through the whole route.
  • If the marked trip matches a saved typical route, the entry gets its name right away; if not, you can save it as a new, one-off entry.
jak.sec_planer:
🧭 Journey plannerbeta

Finds connections between any two stations across the whole PLK network — not just your favorites — including changes (even several), based on the same timetable as the board. It's still a module under testing, so imperfections can happen.

  • Each leg of a result is a clickable card styled like a board row — clicking it opens the full train run.
  • Under Advanced you can set the minimum change time (3 min by default), turn on “Direct only” (no changes), force a specific “via” station or exclude chosen operators.
  • 💾 Save keeps the result to review later in the “Saved results” panel.
  • 📋 To journal adds each leg of the result as a separate entry to the travel plan in the journal — from there, after the actual trip, you'll confirm the real time and delay.
jak.sec_dziennik:
📓 Travel journal

A history of your trips — with the actual time and delay at the boarding and exit stations, not just the plan.

  • Favorite routes — save the stations of a recurring trip once (e.g. your daily commute), and the journal will recognise a matching service and offer to save it under the right name. With “➕ Add another route” you can add as many as you like, including with a change (Leg 2).
  • Travel plan — entries waiting for confirmation: from a train run (mark 🚏/🏁 and “📋 To plan”) or from the planner (“📋 To journal”). When the train actually arrives, come back and click “✅ Confirm” (the trip moves to the entries below) or “❌ Reject”.
  • Saved trips — a list of entries with date, times and delay; edits (e.g. adding kilometres) save automatically, with no separate “Save” button.
  • Export ⬇️ XLSX — download your whole history as a spreadsheet, e.g. for settling a season ticket or your own statistics.
jak.sec_profil:
👤 Profile — sync across devices

Without a profile everything (favorite stations and trains, the journal) is saved only in this one browser. A profile lets you have the same on several devices — with no login, password or e-mail.

  • The profile is a random token — create it once, and on another device simply paste the same token to load the same data.
  • “Unlink device” removes the token only from the phone/computer you're clicking on — the data in the cloud stays and can still be loaded with the same token anywhere else.
  • The token works like a key — whoever has it can load your profile, so don't share it.
jak.sec_prywatnosc:
🔒 Privacy

We don't store IP addresses or any personal data. A profile (if you create one) holds only your own settings: favorite stations, trains and routes in the journal — nothing else. The full description, including the only technical exception (a temporary, irreversible IP hash when a profile is created), is in the GDPR and privacy section.
jak.footnote:
Timetable and delay data come from the public PLK API. This app is not an official PKP or PLK service.
Have a question that isn't answered here? Write to us.

kontakt.title: 💬 Feedback and contact
kontakt.subtitle: Found a bug or have an idea? Write — I'll open a ready e-mail message for you.
kontakt.msgPh: What happened? What should work differently?
kontakt.withInfo: Attach technical details (they help reproduce the problem). There's no name, address or profile token in them.
kontakt.hint: The message opens in your e-mail app (you send it yourself, from your own address). If nothing opens, use “Copy text” and paste it into an e-mail.
kontakt.long: The message is long — if your e-mail app doesn't open, use “Copy text”.
kontakt.copied: Copied. Paste it into a new e-mail.
kontakt.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select and copy the text manually.
kontakt.notConfigured: The contact address isn't configured yet — the form is temporarily inactive.
kontakt.fetchFailed: Couldn't fetch the contact address. Please try again later.
kontakt.rodo1: We don't store IP addresses or any personal data. The only exception: when a new profile is created, the IP address is briefly turned into an irreversible hash, solely to limit the number of profiles created from one place within a day — the hash itself can't be used to recover the address and is deleted automatically after 2 days.
kontakt.rodo2: If you create a profile — voluntarily, without logging in or giving an e-mail — we store under its token only your own settings: favorite stations, favorite trains and favorite routes in the travel journal. Nothing else: no name, address or browsing history.
kontakt.rodoReviewNote: Translation of the Polish source text — to be reviewed by the site owner; the Polish version prevails.

guard.title: 🛡️ Guarded connections
guard.subtitle: I watch your changes. If a delay puts a change at risk, you'll get a notification and an alternative.

guard.altNote: You can't get to {dest} any earlier: the next connection arrives at {arr}. Leaving at {dep} is the latest that still makes it — earlier trains from {from} work too, but you'll wait longer for the change.
guard.empty:
You're not guarding any connection yet.
In the planner tap “🛡️ Guard” next to a result — or add a trip to the plan in the journal.
